samples.summary: Slides band rewrites a numeric-string `listLevel` to 0 (and deletes a numeric-string `fontSize`) instead of coercing — silently flattens stored list nesting / font sizes on PUT
samples.evidence: `bandSlideBlockNumerics` does `block.listLevel = normalizeListLevel(asFiniteNumber(block.listLevel))`, and `asFiniteNumber` returns `undefined` for anything that is not `typeof 'number'`, so `normalizeListLevel(undefined)` → 0. The same pattern in `normalizeSlideInlines` (line 1206) does `delete style.fontSize` for a string size. Nothing in the slides arm validates these two fields as numbers (`assertValidBlockStyle` covers only BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS on `style`, and inline styles are only checked to be objects), so `{"type":"list-item","listLevel":"2"}` and `{"style":{"fontSize":"24"}}` are accepted payloads. Both previously survived verbatim and rendered/exported correctly by JS numeric coercion — packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:95 (touched by this same diff) explicitly documents that a string `listLevel` reaches the exporter and is why `Number(...)` there is 'load-bearing'. After this change the PUT stores level 0 / no fontSize, so a GET→PUT round-trip of such a deck permanently loses the nesting and the size, and the pptx comment's stated premise is no longer true. Coercing with `Number(value)` before banding would repair rather than destroy.

samples.summary: `parseColumnWidthsAttr` drops out-of-band entries, shifting every later column index and shrinking `numCols` so a whole column's cells stop being laid out
samples.evidence: `if (ratio === undefined) continue;` drops the entry instead of pushing a placeholder. `columnWidths.length` is `computeTableLayout`'s `numCols` (view/table-layout.ts:153), and the row `cells` arrays are unchanged, so `cols='1e400,0.5'` yields `[0.5]` → numCols 1 while each row still has 2 cells: column 1's cell content is never laid out, never registered in `blockParentMap`, and the widths line up with the wrong columns. The sibling path deliberately does the opposite — `normalizeColumnRatio`'s own doc (line 240) and the slides validator map an unusable ratio to `0` "so the later columns do not shift" — so the two boundaries now disagree on the same data.

samples.summary: `parseColumnWidthsAttr('')`/absent `cols` now yields `[]` (numCols 0) where the old open-coded parse yielded `[0]`
samples.evidence: `if (!attr) return [];` replaces `(attrs.cols ?? '').split(',').map(Number).filter(n => !isNaN(n))`, which produced `[0]` for an empty/absent attribute (`Number('') === 0`). A table node written without a `cols` attribute therefore materializes with `columnWidths: []`, so `computeTableLayout`'s `for (c = 0; c < numCols; c++)` never runs: no cells are laid out, no `blockParentMap` entries are registered for the cell blocks, and the cell content is unreachable to hit-testing. Degenerate either way, but the failure mode changed from 'zero-width column' to 'no columns at all'.

samples.summary: `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` crams the entire remainder of a genuinely tall row into one overflowing fragment
samples.evidence: `if (++fragments >= MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN) fragHeight = remaining;` makes the 200th fragment absorb all leftover height. For a poisoned height that is the intent, but a *legitimate* table row taller than ~200 pages (one cell holding ~10,000 lines — reachable in a real document that uses a table for layout) now emits a final fragment hundreds of pages tall that overflows its page, so all content past page 200 of that row paints outside the page box / on top of later content instead of being paginated. The bound is on fragments rather than on content, so there is no fallback that keeps the tail readable.

samples.summary: Paste sanitizer bands fontSize/lineHeight/padding/rowHeights/image but leaves `columnWidths` magnitude (and count) unbanded, contrary to the stated 'agree with the CRDT readers' contract
samples.evidence: `for (let c = 0; c < cols; c++) columnWidths.push(asNumber(rawWidths[c]) ?? 1 / cols);` accepts any finite ratio, while the CRDT readers now clamp the same field into `[0, MAX_COLUMN_RATIO]` via `parseColumnWidthsAttr`/`normalizeColumnRatio` and cap the count at `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS`. A pasted payload with `columnWidths: [1e9]` (or a row of 100k cells, since `cols = Math.max(...rows.map(r => r.cells.length))` is unbounded) is persisted into the CRDT unaltered and multiplied straight into geometry — exactly the producer/reader divergence the file's new comments say the bands exist to close.
searchedFor: read clipboard.ts sanitizeTableData / sanitizeCell / sanitizeBlockStyle in full
read normalizeTableMerges in model/types.ts (confirms spans are grid-clamped, widths are not)

samples.summary: Slides band does not apply `isPaintableImageSize` to an inline `style.image`, though a slide text body passes no codec on read
samples.evidence: `normalizeSlideInlines` now bands `style.fontSize` only. Both CRDT readers (model/crdt-tree.ts and frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts) additionally drop an inline image whose width/height is non-finite or above `MAX_IMAGE_SIZE`, and an image height becomes a line height exactly as a font size does. Because a slides text body is stored verbatim, `{"style":{"image":{"src":"x","width":1e9,"height":Infinity}}}` (JSON cannot spell Infinity, but 1e309 parses to it in some parsers, and 1e9 is trivially expressible) is stored and reaches `computeLayout` for every viewer of the deck — the same sink the rest of this walk was added to close.
searchedFor: read normalizeSlideInlines and bandSlideBlockNumerics in docs-content.controller.ts
grep image in docs-content.controller.ts slides arm

finding.summary: Slides band rewrites a numeric-string `listLevel` to 0 (and deletes a numeric-string `fontSize`) instead of coercing — silently flattens stored list nesting / font sizes on PUT

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. `asFiniteNumber` (docs-content.controller.ts:1002-1004) returns undefined for any non-`number`, so `bandSlideBlockNumerics` line 1036 turns a string `listLevel` into `normalizeListLevel(undefined)` = 0 (list-level.ts:43-47), and `normalizeSlideInlines` lines 1206-1208 `delete`s a string `fontSize` (normalizeFontSize(undefined) -> undefined, numeric-attrs.ts:111-115). Nothing rejects these payloads first: assertValidBlockStyle (lines 388-435) only checks alignment, BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS = ['lineHeight','marginTop','marginBottom','textIndent','marginLeft'] (crdt-attrs.ts:42-48) and the boolean spacing markers; `listLevel` appears nowhere else in the controller, inline styles are only checked to be objects (lines 1194-1202), and the PUT handler takes `@Body() body: unknown` with hand-rolled validation only (lines 162-196). The repo's own pptx exporter comment (slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:88-99) documents that a string `listLevel` is stored verbatim by this PUT arm, reaches the exporter, and that without `Number(...)` coercion it "would flatten to 0 and the exported deck would lose its nesting silently" — and every other reader repairs by coercing (crdt-tree.ts:282, yorkie-doc-store.ts:533, clipboard.ts:397), contradicting bandSlideBlockNumerics' own docstring claim (lines 1021-1025) that it applies "the same repair every reader would have applied" and keeps a GET->edit->PUT round-trip working. Silent, permanent loss of stored list nesting / font size on a write path: in-lane correctness/data-loss, no guard, not out of scope.
